system:
You generate one self-contained, executable Modelica model.
Return Modelica code only, without markdown or prose. Use explicit SI units,
parameters, initial conditions, and observable state variables. Prefer simple
equations and Modelica Standard Library components demonstrated by the examples.
The top-level model must compile in OpenModelica. Standalone plant requests must
be directly simulatable and exportable as an FMI 2.0 Co-Simulation FMU. Prefer
scalar, explicitly Real-valued equations when an array reduction or ambiguous
overload could prevent OpenModelica FMU code generation. Give dynamic states
finite, non-singular initial conditions, and give any norm used as a divisor a
well-defined zero-error branch. Controller-only FMI requests must
instead preserve the declared top-level input/output causalities and must not
invent plant dynamics.
Never copy numeric values from retrieved examples into the requested artifact;
only the requirement and its grounded IR are sources of factual values. A model
must not contain unbound parameters: omit unresolved behavior and label it in a
comment instead of fabricating a binding or blocking code generation.
human:
Generate one complete Modelica model for this requirement:
Specify a electromechanical robotic actuator system called BLDCWheelSpeedC around field-oriented or current-limited speed regulation. Its objective is to accelerate to a declared output speed, hold it, and decelerate to rest. Use a maximum command magnitude of 44.2 V-DC-bus, and inject a controlled 10.8 N-or-N.m load torque disturbance during the middle third. The plant must be represented explicitly: A 48 V three-phase permanent-magnet motor with four pole pairs drives a 0.12 m wheel through a 9:1 gearbox and is supplied by a battery with internal resistance. A field-oriented inverter controls phase current. Feedback and evidence come from the following instrumentation: Use phase or armature current, rotor position, output speed, and DC-bus sensing. Include gearbox efficiency, mechanical friction, battery droop, and rotating inertia. Run at 125 Hz for 12 s and retain synchronized state, command, and sensor traces. Require voltage, current, speed, acceleration, state-of-charge, and thermal bounds, primary tracking error below 0.263 rad/s-or-m/s after 7.8 s, and no NaN or infinite physical, control, or estimator values. Treat facts not stated in this request as unknown rather than inventing them.
